User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user within the LinkFlow application, primarily for linking learning resources.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

Tag.title: Tag
Tag.description: Represents a reusable tag used for categorizing learning links.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Tag entity.

name.description: The textual name of the tag (e.g., 'Programming', 'AI', 'Video').

LearningLink.title: LearningLink
LearningLink.description: Represents a single learning resource (e.g., article, video) managed by the LinkFlow application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the LearningLink entity.

title.description: The title of the learning link.

url.description: The URL of the learning resource.

description.description: A summary or description of the learning link, potentially AI-generated.

tagIds.description: References to Tag entities associated with this learning link. (Relationship: LearningLink N:N Tag)

isCompleted.description: Indicates whether the user has marked this learning link as completed.

color.description: The visual theme color chosen for the link card.

icon.description: The icon representing the type of learning resource (e.g., Book, Video, Globe).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the learning link was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the learning link was last updated.

userId.description: Reference to the User who owns this learning link. (Relationship: User 1:N LearningLink)

params.description: The unique ID of the user who owns this learning link.

definition.description: Stores globally available tags for categorizing learning links. These tags can be accessed and selected by all users. Write access can be restricted.

params.description: The unique ID of the tag.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for LinkFlow prioritizes Authorization Independence and Query-Aware Security Rules (QAPs) through systematic denormalization and structural segregation. 

**Authorization Independence:**
1.  **User-Owned Learning Links:** Learning links are stored in a subcollection under each user's document at `/users/{userId}/learningLinks/{learningLinkId}`. Crucially, each `LearningLink` document also contains a `userId` field that explicitly references its owner. This design means that Firestore security rules can verify ownership by checking `request.auth.uid == userId` against the path parameter (e.g., `match /users/{userId}/learningLinks/{learningLinkId} { allow read, write: if request.auth.uid == userId; }`) or the document's `userId` field, **without** needing to perform an expensive and non-atomic `get()` operation on a parent user document. This makes rules simpler, more robust, and highly debuggable.
2.  **Global Roles (Admin):** Administrative roles are managed via a dedicated top-level collection, `/roles_admin/{userId}`. The mere existence of a document at `/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid)` indicates admin status. Checking admin status still involves a `get()` call (e.g., `get(/databases/$(database)/documents/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid)).exists()`), but this is a sanctioned pattern for global role checks that are largely independent of specific data entities and can be cached by the rules engine.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
1.  **Secure Listing of Learning Links:** By segregating learning links into `/users/{userId}/learningLinks`, `list` operations become inherently secure and performant. A user can only `list` documents within their own `/users/$(request.auth.uid)/learningLinks` path. The security rules can then simply ensure that the `userId` in the path matches `request.auth.uid`, guaranteeing that all documents returned by a query satisfy the user's authorization without requiring client-side filtering.
2.  **Global Tags:** Tags are stored in a top-level collection `/tags/{tagId}`. These are assumed to be globally readable, facilitating universal search and categorization. Write access might be limited to authenticated users (for creating new tags during link creation) or administrators. This global scope allows for efficient `list` operations for all users, as there are no user-specific authorization constraints on reading tags.
3.  **Structural Segregation:** The separation of user-owned data (`/users/{userId}/learningLinks`) from global data (`/tags`) and authorization data (`/roles_admin`) ensures that each collection has a homogeneous security posture, simplifying security rule logic and enhancing debuggability.
